change.description: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Under V2, deleting a client leaves its permission resource behind
findings.body: The listener now does nothing unless the V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is on. That avoids the `UnsupportedOperationException` from `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193). But with V2 enabled, nothing replaces it: when a client is deleted, the resource named after its id (created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`/`resolveClient`) stays in the admin-permissions resource server, and so do the scope permissions that point to it. `getClientsWithPermission` will keep returning the deleted id. Consider deleting the V2 resource, or removing the deleted client from its permissions, on `ClientRemovedEvent` when V2 is on. A side effect of the same guard: role and group removal cleanup no longer runs when V1 is off, which it used to do.

findings.title: Unused private method and import
findings.body: Nothing calls `getEvaluationContext(...)`, because `canExchangeTo` throws. The static import of `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` (line 46) is also unused. Removing both also drops the `ClientModelIdentity`/`DefaultEvaluationContext`/`EvaluationContext` imports.

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods says "Returns true"
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireView()` (line 96) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100) says they return `true`. Both are `void` and throw `ForbiddenException`. Reword them to match the other `require*` docs, e.g. "Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false". The `canList()` doc also mentions QUERY_USERS, which matches ClientPermissions.java:243, so that one is fine.

contracts.action: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, so V2 admin permission evaluation now covers clients
contracts.equivalent_path: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission: resource lookup with a fallback to the type resource
contracts.before_after: Before and after resolving a resource, it mirrors UserPermissionsV2:121-126: it falls back to the all-clients resource and returns false when no policy is attached to it
contracts.visible_effect: Admin REST client endpoints allow or forbid access based on V2 scope permissions on the Clients resource type
contracts.failure_mode: getResourceTypeResource returns null when the schema isn't supported. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2

contracts.action: Removal listener now runs only when the V1 FGAP feature is enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous listener, which ran unconditionally
contracts.before_after: Before: cleanup ran on every role, client or group removal. After: it is skipped unless V1 is on, and there is no V2 cleanup
contracts.visible_effect: Stale V2 resources and permissions remain after a client is deleted
contracts.failure_mode: Orphaned authorization data, with no error shown

contracts.action: Test calls switch from the instance helpers getScopePermissionsResource()/createPermission(permission) to the static helpers that take the inherited ManagedClient `client`
contracts.equivalent_path: AbstractPermissionTest.getScopePermissionsResource(client) returns client.admin().authorization().permissions().scope(). createPermission(client, rep) creates the permission and asserts 201 CREATED, the same as the old instance helpers did with the same injected client.
contracts.before_after: Each call passes the same field `client` that is injected into AbstractPermissionTest with @InjectClient(attachTo = ADMIN_PERMISSIONS_CLIENT_ID), so the requests target the same resource as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Test-only change. Behaviour and assertions stay the same.
contracts.failure_mode: If creation does not return 201, createPermission fails the test, the same as before.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** Part 1 adds a Clients resource type and ClientPermissionsV2. The V2 evaluation follows the existing UserPermissionsV2 pattern. Three non-blocking findings. The changed removal listener now runs only when the V1 feature is on, so under V2 nothing cleans up a deleted client's permission resource. ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private method and import. Two javadocs on void require* methods say they return true.

**Batch 2 of 2.** This part changes only `UserResourceTypePermissionTest.java`, and the change is mechanical: every call now uses the static helpers, which take a `client` argument (`getScopePermissionsResource(client)` and `createPermission(client, …)`). The calls pass the same injected `client` field as before, and the static helpers in `AbstractPermissionTest` do what the old instance helpers did. I found nothing to flag.
